Hi Eli (and team),

Thanks for the sync today — good conversation. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum on the Private (air-gapped) option you expressed interest in. High-level from our side: Redwood supports three deployment profiles (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private VPC / on-prem). Based on what you described — no internet egress from the cluster and strict change-window controls — Private on-prem (air-gapped) is the right path.

Call highlights / outstanding clarifications:
- Hardware: you confirmed the target racks are 2x DGX-style chassis per site with an existing VMware layer. Please confirm exact GPU model/driver matrix (we asked for node-level inventory).
- Upgrade policy: you asked whether Redwood can perform in-place OS/kernel/agent upgrades in a fully-offline environment, or if we ship offline update bundles for your SREs to apply.
- Maintenance windows: you prefer quarterly maintenance windows with a 4-hour blackout period and a 2-hour candidate prep window.
- Spares / rollback: we discussed spare-node requirements and rollback image availability.

Attachments: Redwood_OnPrem_Checklist_v2.pdf (inventory + network test checklist). Please fill out sections A–C and return.

2) Marissa to confirm offline upgrade options and provide a sample MOP (target: Thu 2/17).
3) Ben to schedule a 30‑min ops deep-dive for Wed 2/23 with your SRE + our deployment lead.

If any of the action items/timing don't work, tell me and I’ll adjust.

Eli — short answers up front, then specifics.

1) Offline upgrades: yes, Redwood supports signed offline update bundles. We produce a signed tarball that contains the agent, runtime libs, and an OS package list. The bundle also includes a verification manifest (SHA256) and a PGP signature you can verify with our public key. Your SREs can apply the bundle per an MOP; Redwood can optionally do a supervised apply in a physically isolated mode if you want an extra hand (on-site eng fee).

2) Rollback images: we supply immutable rollback images and a signed manifest. Images are versioned and validated in our CI; we also provide a validation script your SREs can run locally (hash check + runtime smoke tests included in the bundle). You retain the image on local media — Redwood will not remotely modify that artifact in an air-gapped deployment unless expressly scheduled and signed by your change board.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Image size: the typical runtime image is ~40GB; plan for local media and staging server with 100GB free.
- Spares: recommend 1 hot spare per 12 production nodes for quick RA/replace; we'll include exact part numbers in the BOM.
- UPS/Shutdown: nodes tolerate a clean shutdown, but unclean power loss risks data corruption for local caches — we recommend UPS with 10-minute hold for all control-plane racks.
- Maintenance cadence: we can support quarterly security patching; major model/quant rollouts we treat as separate change windows.

Attached is a first-draft MOP for offline upgrades: Airgap_Patch_MOP.docx (contains steps, verification, rollback). We'll update it with your inventory once received.

Action items I can own: produce a short offline-upgrade SOW paragraph you can attach to procurement (by Thu 2/17). Ben — I’ll sync with you on the SRE resources for the ops deep-dive.

—Marissa
